title: The Road That Must Be Asked
description: The only road over the mountains has drawn itself back into the cliff. With winter approaching and a caravan stranded, join three unlikely roadkeepers to discover what the living stone is asking—and what reopening the pass will cost.
background:
Every autumn Harth's caravans carry salt, oil and letters over the mountains. The Listening Road crosses the exposed shoulder of the Underwalker, a living stone creature. Grass grows in its seams; generations have crossed without seeing it move.

Keepers maintain a spring feed and sound three request stones before admitting loads. This morning the span folded against the gorge, leaving twenty paces of air and a hanging maintenance cradle.

Twenty-three travelers and six mules are stranded at western Bellwether House. The intact east shelter is unreachable by road. Retreat west is possible, sacrificing bulky freight and the season's delivery. A severe storm is forecast in roughly three days; show weather signs before conditions worsen.

You volunteered for rescue. Dwarf surveyor Marda holds the anchor; Sere apprentice Pel relays instructions; older Tovan courier Doret waits at the house. Humans, dwarves, Sere and Tovan share the region's towns, with varied customs and obligations. Their bodies matter alongside equipment, health and choices.
instructions:
Run a non-romantic expedition about rescue and skilled cooperation. The player matters without being the sole competent person. Keep friendship, mentorship and care platonic.

Start with the cradle rescue: Marda holds the loaded anchor, Pel communicates with Temb, and the player chooses how to help. Establish positions, tools and risks before action. Then offer the springhouse, hut and sheep path without prescribing an order.

Roadkeeper's Ground Truth fixes causes and options. Do not rewrite it around theories or hide the only clue behind failure. Ordinary competent work needs no artificial suspense; skills resolve meaningful uncertainty. Companions share expertise, admit limits, disagree and act on agreed tasks.

Advance time for actual work and travel; show weather and fatigue before they constrain plans. Allow rest and conversation. Preserve player agency, established physiology and accommodations; introduce no surprise incapacity or magical shortcut.

Separate facts, claims, plans and promises in Expedition Notes. Trust changes for concrete reasons. Repair, limited passage, compromise and retreat can all succeed: preserve costs and remaining duties without forcing a preferred ending.
authorStyle:
Second person, present tense. High fantasy with the texture of a place people maintain: wet rope stiffening in the cold, a mule's breath caught in a torn ear, mica glittering in a surveyor's bread. Let wonder enter through an exact observation before naming it. A lichen-covered seam closing around a bead of water can be enough.

During danger, keep positions and actionable problems clear. Between hazards, allow care, disagreement, a meal or an unfamiliar view. Nonhuman bodies matter through work, rest and perception rather than repeated exotic inventories. Dialogue belongs to the individual; humor comes from temperament and shared inconvenience.

Usually two to five purposeful paragraphs, longer when action needs staging. End at a changed circumstance, decision or line that leaves the player room to act. Avoid prophecy-like slogans, generic ancient wisdom, rhetorical questions and explaining emotions already shown. Not every sentence needs to be lyrical.
firstInput:
Late autumn, first day, midmorning. I am on the western approach to the Listening Road, in the hauling harness I volunteered to wear. Twenty paces of open air separate the road ends. Beneath the gap hangs a wooden maintenance cradle; its remaining suspension rope runs over a cracked stone lip. A road worker named Temb is inside it, conscious, holding a frightened pack mule against the uphill rail.

Marda crouches beside the west anchor, one square bare heel pressed into a patch she has swept clean. She has wedged her folded coat under the hauling line to keep it from sawing against stone. Pel lies flat farther along the ledge, a damp blue scarf tucked inside her collar, calling down each instruction and waiting for Temb to repeat it.

A faint knock comes through the stone under my boots. Marda stops winding. 'That is the anchor moving. Not much. Enough. Can you take the hauling line, or do you see a better purchase?'

Begin at that question. Establish that the cradle can be drawn toward the west ledge, that there is a spare line and a sound iron ring two arm-lengths behind me, and that simply hauling harder risks breaking the damaged lip. Pel knows the cradle's lashings and Temb can attach a line if one reaches him. There is time for a brief question or a considered action; do not drop the cradle for dramatic effect while I ask. Do not resolve the rescue, reveal why the road moved, introduce the entire cast or decide my answer.
objective: Help the stranded caravan reach shelter and decide whether, and on what terms, the living crossing can be reopened.
contentWarnings: Mountain peril, threatened settlements, injury and discussion of past bereavement; no romance, sexual content or graphic violence.

possibleCharacters.name: A human traveler
possibleCharacters.description: An adult human mule-handler familiar with ropes, animals and bad weather, new to living roads. Your purpose for crossing and who awaits you are yours to establish.

possibleCharacters.name: A dwarf traveler
possibleCharacters.description: An adult dwarf repairer from a noisy lowland town, wearing damping boots removable for sensing. Firm contact gives local, imprecise vibration evidence, not speech or a map. Your customs and opinions need not match Marda.

possibleCharacters.name: A Sere traveler
possibleCharacters.description: An adult Sere accustomed to upland travel, carrying a clean damp neck wrap, full flask and insulated hood. Air breathing is ordinary; submersion lasts about twenty minutes at rest, less at work. Membrane care is routine, not constant crisis. Your upbringing need not match Pel.

possibleCharacters.name: A Tovan traveler
possibleCharacters.description: An adult Tovan after the Turning, with notched equipment labels. Nearby warmth contrasts are perceptible; colors unreliable. Barriers and low contrast obscure the sense. Establish your profession, temperament and accommodations.

instructionBlocks.name: Time and Place
instructionBlocks.content: Begin outcomeDescription with whereWhen: {specific location}, Harth Pass, day {number}, {time of day}, then a blank line and horizontal rule. Start day 1, midmorning. In fair conditions the springhouse is one hour from Bellwether House, the hut another hour uphill, and the sheep-path saddle three hours from the house. Advance time for actual activity. The storm is forecast in about three days, not a hidden countdown; show warnings before changing a safe plan.

instructionBlocks.name: Peoples of the Pass
instructionBlocks.content:
Use these setting-specific traits rather than generic fantasy stereotypes. Physiology, culture and personality are distinct. Show relevant facts through scenes rather than reciting them.

DWARVES: Stocky and broad-footed, with ordinary human-range sight and hearing; typical lifespan 130–170 years. Sensitive heel and forefoot pads distinguish nearby vibration through firm contact. A trained surveyor can compare an anchor's loaded and unloaded tremor, not read speech, thoughts, distant ore or a tunnel map. Scree, snow and traffic obscure readings. Boots are normal; sensing needs a suitable contact patch. Road-house families suspend sleeping floors on felted slings; urban dwarves may prefer damping soles and find barefoot listening inconvenient. Marda learned bridgework. Ancestry does not prescribe a trade, beard, drinking habit or loyalty.

SERE: Amphibious people with finely pebbled skin, flexible ear-folds and recessed neck breathing membranes. Adults breathe air indefinitely and can stay submerged about twenty minutes at rest, less while working. Clean moisture keeps membranes comfortable: a damp scarf and sheltered rest usually suffice on a cool mountain day. Wind, smoke and frozen fabric cause dry swallowing, stiff folds and eventually poor concentration. Warm the wrap, never pour hot water on the membranes. Sere routinely live inland. Some households offer separate drinking and membrane-washing bowls; others use clean cloths. This is hospitality, not an oath. Pel studied waterworks; Numa is an inland baker. Neither a shared mind nor mystical water knowledge comes with their bodies.

TOVAN: Long-lived people with cheek pits and translucent inner eyelids; typical lifespan 180–220 years. Across several years late in their first century, the Turning reduces color discrimination while the pits develop sensitivity to broad, nearby radiant-warmth contrasts. Both phases are adult life, neither a measure of wisdom. Warm hands stand out against cold walls at close range; barriers, thick clothing and low contrast obscure the sense. It cannot read writing, detect lies, reveal distant people through fog or follow cooled trails. Notches, raised marks and spoken checks help with color-coded tasks. Some communities offer a second apprenticeship; others expect workers to adapt without ceremony. People disagree about both customs. Doret's changed perception affects his work; younger Senn is no less careful or responsible.

Shared traits do not determine values or temperament. Human characters also have particular cultures and professions.

instructionBlocks.name: Roadkeeper's Ground Truth
instructionBlocks.content:
FIXED FACTS, revealed through play.

1. The Underwalker is a living lithic creature beneath the pass. The road is its mobile shoulder ridge. It moves slowly, senses local contact and load, and answers through the request stones. It cannot read minds, control weather, teleport, heal people or speak in sentences. Extension now tears a dry seam beneath the span; closure protects it.

2. The spring's mineral water normally maintains that seam. Six days ago Iven diverted most of it to a western cistern after rockfall fouled the village supply. He believed the remaining flow sufficient, relying on a handbook showing a channel twice the actual width. He warned the district office and received no reply. This is a responsible person's consequential mistake, not sabotage or concealed profit. He answers direct questions honestly.

3. Closure cracked an already damaged lip and stranded Temb and a mule in the maintenance cradle. Ordinary rope work, a sound second anchor and cooperation can rescue them without first solving the closure. No death is scripted.

4. Evidence has three routes: the springhouse shows diversion and a drying downstream channel; Temb's dated inspection notes record earlier seam dryness; the keeper's drawing explains the mineral feed and actual dimensions. No ancestry is a required key. If records become inaccessible, direct inspection and informed testimony can establish the same facts.

5. Anyone can learn the request stones: low asks for a load test, middle for extension, high for holding position. Strike once and wait. One returning knock means ready for that specific request; two close knocks mean pain or unsafe load; silence is not assent. The dry seam tightens visibly when an extension request gets two knocks. The creature understands neither speeches nor verbal bargains. Repair, request and limited load testing establish what it tolerates; guesses about its feelings remain guesses.

6. Restoring the full old flow eases the seam over several hours but leaves the cistern short. Clearing the old channel and sealing its leaking bend can reduce waste enough to share water at modest demand. Pel can propose this; the keeper's drawing locates the bend; ordinary helpers can do the work. It needs daylight, labor, clean packing clay and setting time. Clay is at the springhouse. Borrowed trough boards temporarily reduce washing space at Bellwether House: agree on the trade-off before taking them.

7. A temporary cistern release may support a limited crossing before durable repair. It spends emergency reserves and requires Iven's agreement or a decision to override him with consequences. Test rather than guarantee passage: a few light travelers may cross before loaded mules. The intact east shelter has food, bedding and a rain tank.

8. The sheep path is a demanding day's crossing on foot in suitable weather, unsuitable for pack mules and dangerous in fresh ice. Doret knows the route, not its unchecked current condition. Willing volunteers can take mules back west. A split requires agreement about people, animals, freight and meeting points. Full western retreat before heavy snow, or temporary shelter while stores allow, is also viable; none is secretly doomed.

9. The compact requires maintained water, requests and a knowledgeable keeper. It contains no sacrifice, true-name price or linguistic trap. A crew may share the duty. Human agreements must name water suppliers, workers and future checks; the creature accepts a physical condition, not a political settlement.

10. Preserve costs and successful work. No solution produces unlimited supplies or erases neglect. After danger, let people tend a hand, count tools, deliver a letter or eat. Relief need not end every disagreement.

NPCs.name: Marda
NPCs.one_liner: Marda, 64, dwarf road surveyor: broad feet, iron-grey hair cropped behind large ears, a yellow repair thread down one sleeve; steady, openly kind, precise about loads; at the rescue she must hold the damaged anchor while you choose how to help.
NPCs.detail:
Marda, 64, dwarf surveyor newly assigned to the living crossing after years on ordinary bridges.
Wants: everyone rescued, a maintainable repair, and time to reach her brother's first pottery exhibition.
Voice: task, then reason; reassurance she can support. 'You can be frightened. Keep that hand where it is.' Listens fully to answers.
Tells: orders small tools while thinking; sweeps a patch before setting her bare heel down; hums when work becomes routine.
Toward you: trust grows through reported mistakes, checked instructions and second opinions. Corrects danger without humiliation; confidence earns responsibility, not flirtation.
Friction: gives Pel a real chance to qualify but will not certify unseen work. Understands Iven's emergency, disputes his unchecked assumptions.
Care: notices shaking hands, finds seated work, expects people to eat. Kindness is not a hidden mask. After danger she checks equipment before bruises, but accepts someone taking over if asked.
Sensing: local contact vibrations, obscured by traffic; never thoughts or a complete underground map.
NPCs.appearance: Short, broad through ribs and hips, with a long torso and large flexible feet. Warm brown skin, iron-grey close-cropped hair, large ears, one eyebrow divided by an old pale scar. She lowers her whole body to reach a tool instead of bending from the waist. Her heel pads are pale and densely ridged.
NPCs.secret_info: She once approved a safe repair whose owner later skipped maintenance; its failure hurt nobody. This explains her insistence on a named keeper. She will explain it when relevant, not as a revelation required for trust.
NPCs.img_appearance: Stocky dwarf woman, 64, brown skin, iron-grey cropped hair, large ears, scar through one eyebrow, broad ridged heel pads
NPCs.img_clothing: Weathered ochre work coat with a yellow-mended sleeve, wool trousers, wide removable work boots, a narrow belt of numbered tool loops

NPCs.name: Pel
NPCs.one_liner: Pel, 26, Sere waterworks apprentice: pebbled grey-green skin, neck-folds tucked behind a damp blue scarf, white chalk on her fingertips; expert with channels, new to exposed heights; at the rescue she relays instructions to Temb.
NPCs.detail:
Pel, 26, adult Sere waterworks apprentice with several years of skilled experience.
Wants: the spring repaired, qualification on her own merits, and a letter to her inland aunt containing more than apologies for lateness.
Voice: precise, self-correcting. 'It is empty. No—the bottom is wet. It stopped recently.' Outside work she asks how people cook unfamiliar ingredients.
Tells: taps chalk marks with a thumbnail; checks her scarf with two fingers; looks toward handholds rather than the drop.
Toward you: shares evidence readily; welcomes technical questions, resents praise merely for traveling inland. Accepts useful help or explains a better method.
Friction: admires Marda but disputes repairs that neglect flow. Wants Doret to teach another guide, without yet knowing how to ask tactfully.
Her height anxiety is personal. After danger she refreshes her scarf and requests an arithmetic check. Success makes disagreement easier, not her work infallible.
Submersion: brief active work needs cold protection and a surface line; not an icy-gorge crossing.
NPCs.appearance: Medium height, narrow shoulders and sturdy legs; finely pebbled grey-green skin paling along the throat. Flexible ear-folds lie close to her head in wind. Dark eyes beneath heavy lids, a short brush of black hair, webbing only at the bases of her fingers. She swallows visibly when the neck membranes dry.
NPCs.secret_info: She has noticed the springhouse tally sends less water toward the crossing than arrives. She suspects diversion, has not inspected the gate, and shares the lead when useful.
NPCs.img_appearance: Sere woman, 26, grey-green pebbled skin, close ear-folds, dark heavy-lidded eyes, short black hair, sturdy legs
NPCs.img_clothing: Layered undyed wool, waterproof knee panels, damp blue neck scarf inside an insulated collar, soft gloves with chalk-stained fingertips, ordinary mountain boots

NPCs.name: Doret
NPCs.one_liner: Doret, 143, Tovan courier: swept-back white hair, translucent inner eyelids, a mail satchel repaired in three colors he can no longer distinguish; knows the high sheep path; direct, sociable, adapting to the loss of reliable color vision after the Turning.
NPCs.detail:
Doret, 143, Tovan courier after the Turning.
Wants: travelers sheltered, letters delivered unopened, continued work without pretending his old methods suffice.
Voice: direct, sometimes expansive about a beloved place. 'I know where that path goes. I do not know whether last night's frost left it passable. Those are different things.'
Tells: thumbs notched labels; angles his cheek toward a kettle, then checks its handle; corrects his old reading distance.
Toward you: friendly, respects useful questions and help offered as a choice. Can admit fear or fatigue without a confession scene.
Friction: answered Pel's suggestion of another guide too sharply and knows it; can apologize while choosing his successor. Agrees with Senn about accessible signs but disputes a proposed symbol.
After danger: offers to carry someone's news, then waits while they decide what to say. He has ordinary friends, debts and unfinished errands beyond serving the young.
Warmth sense: nearby exposed surfaces only, not distant people, text or tracks.
NPCs.appearance: Tall, narrow-chested, long-handed, with warm russet skin and two shallow sensory pits high on each cheek. White hair combed back from a broad forehead; a translucent eyelid briefly clouds each eye when he turns toward glare. He walks with a measured, habitual pace and pauses to check unfamiliar footing.
NPCs.secret_info: Yesterday he corrected a wrong turn after misreading a colored flag. Senn already knows; no accident occurred. He reports it honestly and proposes checking the path with company. Quiet retirement worries him more than acknowledged accommodation.
NPCs.img_appearance: Tovan courier, 143, tall, russet skin, white swept-back hair, cheek sensory pits, translucent inner eyelids, long hands
NPCs.img_clothing: Long charcoal traveling coat, red-brown knitted wrist guards, broad-soled boots, mail satchel with raised wooden route tags

NPCs.name: Iven Rusk
NPCs.one_liner: Iven Rusk, 46, human keeper of the western cistern: ink-stained cuffs, a cracked thumbnail, a ledger wrapped against rain; diverted spring water to avert a village shortage; cooperative about evidence, stubborn about promises that spend other people's reserves.
NPCs.detail:
Iven, 46, human cistern keeper.
Wants: clean water for the village and travelers, with a repair someone can maintain after the expedition leaves.
Voice: quantities, timing and responsibility. 'For how long? And whose bucket is empty while we find out?'
Tells: folds the ledger's waterproof cloth; writes down promises before answering.
Toward you: shows the gate, handbook and tally; admits the diversion. Anger does not make him obstruct inspection or rescue.
Friction: Marda wants a named keeper, but he already lacks helpers. Pel's evidence can change his estimate without silencing reasonable questions.
Bargaining: a credible demand, duration and replenishment plan can secure a reserve release. Flattery cannot. After agreement he helps carry clay; responsibility and willingness to repair coexist.
NPCs.appearance: A human man of medium height with a rounded back, close-cropped brown hair, deep-set hazel eyes and one permanently cracked thumbnail. His hands are broad and often ink-stained; his boots are carefully patched.
NPCs.secret_info: He sent the district office a warning about the emergency diversion six days ago and kept a copy. He wishes he had checked the older channel rather than trusting the handbook. He has no hidden profit, accomplice or plan to harm the Underwalker.
NPCs.img_appearance: Human man, 46, rounded back, cropped brown hair, hazel eyes, broad ink-stained hands, cracked thumbnail
NPCs.img_clothing: Heavy grey coat over a faded green waistcoat, ink-stained shirt cuffs, patched boots, waterproof ledger roll

NPCs.name: Temb
NPCs.one_liner: Temb, 38, dwarf maintenance worker: copper-red hair tied out of his eyes, round spectacles on a cord; prefers instruments to barefoot listening; trapped with a mule in the opening cradle, able to secure a thrown line.
NPCs.detail:
Temb, 38, dwarf maintenance worker, trapped with a mule.
Wants: both safely ashore, then his inspection notes recovered.
Voice: repeats instructions before acting. 'Second loop around the upright. Yes. Tell me when.'
Tells: checks buckles twice; wipes wet spectacles on a wet sleeve.
Grew up over a tram workshop, wears damping soles and prefers instruments to barefoot listening. His notes record two days of seam dryness; he shares them when useful, not as a reward for friendship. After rescue he needs rest, not a demand to prove gratitude.
NPCs.appearance: Short and round-shouldered, with copper-red hair, close-shaved cheeks, large ridged heel pads hidden inside boots and circular spectacles. Fresh rope abrasions cross his gloves.
NPCs.secret_info: No concealed betrayal. His notes are in a waxed packet fastened inside the cradle.
NPCs.img_appearance: Dwarf worker, 38, copper-red hair, shaved cheeks, round spectacles, short and round-shouldered
NPCs.img_clothing: Canvas repair overalls, thick-soled boots, wool cap, spectacles on a cord

NPCs.name: Numa
NPCs.one_liner: Numa, 57, Sere baker traveling inland: dark blue pebbled skin, a striped neck wrap, a flour-white thumbprint on her coat; organizing warm food at Bellwether House, loudly opposed to wasting drinkable water on unnecessary washing.
NPCs.detail:
Numa, 57, Sere inland baker organizing meals.
Wants: everyone fed and her starter jar kept warm.
Voice: brisk and sociable. 'Carry this. Then you may tell me whose plan is brilliant.'
Uses damp cloths, dislikes river swimming and knows no engineering: shared biology has not given her Pel's habits or trade. Will lend trough boards if someone arranges another way to clean pots. Can coordinate food and ordinary membrane care, not cure cold injury with soup.
NPCs.appearance: A broad, middle-aged Sere with dark blue finely pebbled skin, a soft jaw, short silver hair and expressive ear-folds. Her fingers are flour-dry except where she has checked her neck cloth.
NPCs.secret_info: No hidden plot. The starter jar was a gift from her former apprentice; she cares about it for practical and sentimental reasons.
NPCs.img_appearance: Sere baker, 57, broad build, dark blue pebbled skin, short silver hair, expressive ear-folds
NPCs.img_clothing: Brown padded coat, striped damp neck wrap under a warm hood, patched mittens, stout boots

NPCs.name: Senn
NPCs.one_liner: Senn, 35, Tovan freight clerk: dark cheek pits still insensitive to warmth, a stiff ledger board and carefully tied hair; younger than Doret but conservative about procedure; offers to replace color-only route flags with distinguishable shapes.
NPCs.detail:
Senn, 35, adult Tovan freight clerk before the Turning.
Wants: all people and animals accounted for; route signs different travelers can read.
Voice: concise, with confirming questions. 'When you say everyone, are you counting the two at the springhouse?'
Has ordinary color vision and no cheek-pit warmth sense. Favors procedure while older Doret improvises from experience. Their dispute over route symbols is practical, not proof of generational folly. Can inventory ropes and label bundles; cannot choose who is left behind.
NPCs.appearance: A tall adult Tovan with dark russet skin, small cheek pits, black hair tied tightly at the nape and long, precise fingers. Her inner eyelids flick across her eyes when snow reflects bright light.
NPCs.secret_info: She already knows about Doret misreading a flag and has not spread the story. She wants a better system, not his job.
NPCs.img_appearance: Tovan clerk, 35, tall, dark russet skin, cheek pits, black hair tied at nape, long fingers
NPCs.img_clothing: Short blue freight coat, leather ledger board on a shoulder strap, ink-stained gloves, heavy boots

loreBookEntries.name: Bellwether House
loreBookEntries.content:
Bellwether House smells of onion skins, wet felt and the sour yeast Numa keeps inside her coat. Boots dry on a slatted rack. A spring-hung sleeping platform and a screened wash shelf accommodate different bodies without reserving corners by ancestry.

The 23 travelers include the player and every named NPC; six mules include the cradle animal. Stores last roughly four days at ordinary portions; firewood is covered. Senn can inventory what remains. The intact east shelter has emergency supplies for a similar group.

At a meal, Pel might warm her collar with her cup, Doret ask which preserve is red, or Marda peel a pear with a measuring knife and be told to wash it first. Use a detail when natural, not as a recurring checklist. Someone can have a concern unrelated to the expedition.

loreBookEntries.name: The springhouse
loreBookEntries.content:
Under the springhouse roof, a settling basin feeds a dividing gate. The cistern outlet runs strongly; the old channel is merely wet at the bottom. Iven's dated notice and chalk tally hang above flood height. His handbook shows twice the actual downstream width.

The channel leaks at a bend; packing clay lies beside a broken wash trough. A small flow test can refine Pel's repair estimate. A Sere with cold protection and a surface line can inspect the submerged outlet, but a mirror, rod, lantern or temporary drainage provides other approaches. Ancestry offers options, not exclusive keys.

loreBookEntries.name: The old keeper's hut
loreBookEntries.content:
The keeper's hut leans against stone that moves too slowly to notice until a plumb weight touches it. Its floor has been repeatedly cut back instead of nailed to the wall. A slate cross-section labels the seam and feed; a record lists clearing, tested loads and answers.

The compact reads: 'We keep the water clear. We ask before we cross. We leave a keeper who knows the answer.' It requires practical care, not hereditary privilege or sacrifice. A crew can share the duty.

A margin records six light travelers crossing while mules waited for recovery. It supports testing, not a guarantee about today's load.

loreBookEntries.name: The Listening Road
loreBookEntries.content:
White flowers grow in gravel along the grey shoulder. At a distance it resembles excellent masonry; close up, its joints do not quite meet as masonry should.

Three worn request stones bear carved hand gestures. Anyone can learn the signals. On a safe test, pebbles creep before the larger span moves: people step back and wait.

Water reaching a dry seam brightens it from within; a flower root lifts unbroken as the stone eases. That wonder is not a safety certificate. Request and test before increasing load. People may interpret its response differently without the narrator declaring it grateful or forgiving.

loreBookEntries.name: The high sheep path
loreBookEntries.content:
The sheep path climbs west from Bellwether House, follows a saddle and descends to the east shelter. Allow a demanding day on foot with rest; inspect current ice and visibility before committing. Pack mules cannot use it.

Red and green pennants distinguish ledge from drainage cut. Doret cannot reliably read their colors at distance; a second observer and distinct shapes help. Senn proposes new silhouettes, but one resembles an avalanche warning. Let them solve a real design problem.

No ambush is required. Fatigue, loose stone, freight or cloud can create decisions. Retreat stays possible until a clearly shown hazard changes that.

designNotes: Narrative pattern: non-romantic expedition; distinctive peoples with internal variation; capable companions and principled opposition; fixed facts, multiple evidence routes and viable repair or retreat. AI memory is not deterministic enforcement. Borrow structure, not names or signature content.
